destination: A versioned store and application atlas with one source for decoder names, generated references, privacy-safe drift detection, and measured decoding coverage.
record_scope: Repository criteria for the WR-000439 extension. No production Work Request was created or amended in this desk.

acceptance_criteria.text: Extract plist schemes, document types and roles, activities, supported intents, App Intents actions and parameters, PlugIns, and literal ms-outlook host/path/query-key grammar into spec/outlook/surface-atlas.json. Include version, source hashes, pointers or offsets, uncertainty, and generated reference. Compare versions with structured new/removed/changed output. Test synthetic bundles only.

After PR #2038 lands, maintain spec/outlook/hxstore-atlas.json for every known block and record type and field ID with name, wire type, decoder, proven/inferred/unknown confidence, evidence, and first-seen Outlook version. Distinguish wire IDs, object offsets, string-run selectors, and decoded output names. Unknown IDs remain explicit. hxprobe reads names from this atlas; generate the human reference from it.

Add a synthetic-tested count-only hxprobe command for the orchestrator's private-copy run. Emit only record/block/field IDs, wire types, byte counts and occurrence counts. Never emit strings, payload bytes, identities, hashes of content, paths, or error excerpts from the store. Validate CRC, decompression and object bounds. Orchestrator returns counts; this desk never reads a store.

When PR #2040, wr443-deeplink-grammar and wr443-send-by-id land, bind their exact revisions and merge evidence into surface-atlas.json. Add extraction of routes and query keys assembled from binary constants, with symbol/offset evidence and inferred confidence. Preserve differences between literal grammar, reconstructed grammar and runtime acceptance. No URL invocation or send probe is part of this criterion.

Given an Outlook build, regenerate both atlases and emit one structured diff for new/removed/changed fields, wire types, keys, routes and intents. Preserve first-seen history and compare semantic changes separately from evidence changes. Refuse incompatible schemas, version mismatches, incomplete reads and malformed formats. Store observations must use the count-only contract.

Using synthetic fixtures and orchestrator-returned counts, report decoded-byte percentage and decoded-field-ID percentage by record type. Define denominators and unknown handling, count unique covered byte spans without overlap, report zero denominators as unavailable, and order unknown IDs by frequency with stable tie breaks. Do not substitute message recovery percentage for format-byte coverage.

Design, do not install, a launchd version-change trigger. Read CFBundleVersion, compare with the last successful build, run combined drift, and prepare ./run.sh call report-problem with bounded diff summary and stable idempotency key. Specify missed updates, retries, failures, duplicate suppression and atomic state replacement. No LaunchAgent, profile, preference or credential changes.

slices.name: Combined drift, measured coverage and trigger design

decisions.question: What is slice 1?
decisions.answer: Deliver the independent static bundle baseline and drift. Keep the unmerged hxprobe dependency out of this PR.
decisions.trade_off: The store atlas remains an explicit later criterion.

decisions.question: Are schema.rs names numeric field IDs?
decisions.answer: No. Preserve wire IDs, offsets and heuristic string selectors as distinct concepts.
decisions.trade_off: A field-name list cannot establish byte or ID coverage.

decisions.question: Which module interface?
decisions.answer: Use extract_surface, diff_surface and render_surface with a thin stdout-only CLI and no public extractor registry.
decisions.trade_off: A future binary format may require internal changes. Three independent designs favored keeping format details local.

decisions.question: How are tests and input failures handled?
decisions.answer: Test the module and CLI with generated synthetic app bundles. Require exact CFBundleVersion, refuse malformed metadata, and report skipped symlinks.
decisions.trade_off: Unreadable or unsupported inputs fail instead of producing a partial success.

decisions.question: What counts as drift?
decisions.answer: Compare semantic identities and fields separately from hashes and evidence offsets. Retain all literal offsets.
decisions.trade_off: Consumers must inspect source_changes as well as semantic changes.

decisions.question: How strong is binary grammar evidence?
decisions.answer: In slice 1 extract ASCII ms-outlook literals from identified Mach-O files. Emit host, path and query keys, omit query values, and make no runtime claim.
decisions.trade_off: Routes assembled from constants remain unknown until S3.

decisions.question: What does first seen mean?
decisions.answer: First observed in atlas history. Preserve existing first_seen_version when extracting against a baseline.
decisions.trade_off: This does not claim the version in which Microsoft introduced a declaration.

decisions.question: Where do remaining criteria live?
decisions.answer: Keep the extension criteria and dependency map in this versioned JSON and link them from the PR. Do not mutate the production Work Request under the no-production-writes boundary.
decisions.trade_off: The orchestrator must reconcile these criteria into the Work Request record if needed.

decisions.question: Install a version watcher now?
decisions.answer: No. S4 designs the trigger after combined drift and its count-only contract exist.
decisions.trade_off: No automatic watch runs from slice 1.

decisions.question: How are delivery checks run in the fresh checkout?
decisions.answer: Install the committed Node lockfile and mypy 2.3.0 locally, and invoke the existing leak guard with the absolute repository root used by its hooks.
decisions.trade_off: Local dependency directories remain ignored. No gate, global configuration or dependency manifest changes.

decisions.question: How much work fits this desk session?
decisions.answer: Deliver ATLAS-STORE-SOURCE only, following the explicit one-session-per-criterion sizing. Merge the approved vendor branch into the approved atlas base without rebasing.
decisions.trade_off: The count-only command and grammar reconciliation remain subsequent criteria. This PR stays open against main.

decisions.question: Where do decoder display names live?
decisions.answer: Keep stable decoder_key identities and display names in hxstore-atlas.json. Generate the Key enum, name mapping and iteration list during the Cargo build. Remove the hand-maintained definitions.
decisions.trade_off: A runtime JSON reader would add runtime configuration and parsing. Build generation uses the repository Python 3 standard library and adds no Cargo dependency. Name edits require rebuilding hxprobe.

decisions.question: Which public seams prove the name migration?
decisions.answer: Test the reference CLI and the actual hxprobe map CLI using a generated CRC-valid literal-only LZ4 block. Copy only the maintained crate, generator and atlas into a temporary tree, rename an entry, rebuild and inspect map and tally output.
decisions.trade_off: This proves name locality and build invalidation. It does not establish real-store decoding accuracy or wire-ID coverage.

decisions.question: How are wire IDs and first-seen versions represented?
decisions.answer: Distinguish containers, record anchors, block types, object classes, envelope tags, object byte offsets, string-run selectors and wire field IDs. Keep unknown IDs and first_seen_version explicitly null. Bind interpretation evidence to exact vendor revision and SHA-256.
decisions.trade_off: The pinned implementation establishes recognized layouts and heuristics, not the first Outlook build or empirical proof. All interpreted meanings are inferred and unresolved meanings unknown.

decisions.question: How do malformed atlas edits fail?
decisions.answer: Validate before generating any reference or Rust. Reject duplicate IDs, decoder keys and decoder display names, dangling parents, unsupported schemas, missing evidence and malformed provenance.
decisions.trade_off: Duplicate display names would collapse distinct tally entries. Invalid atlas input stops the Cargo build instead of using fallback names.

decisions.question: Which output contract changes?
decisions.answer: Generate the eight named schema-map labels and their tally keys from the atlas. Stable decoder keys continue to drive extraction. SQLite table and column contracts are separate derived outputs and retain their existing names.
decisions.trade_off: The atlas migration does not rename persisted SQLite columns or modify decoding heuristics.

decisions.question: What fits the next session?
decisions.answer: Finish ATLAS-STORE-PROBE on a new branch from 039a4d05. Include structural coverage requested with the command. Keep ATLAS-GRAMMAR-RECONCILE for the next session.
decisions.trade_off: One session per criterion takes priority over batching both ordered criteria into this PR.

decisions.question: Which public seam and interface?
decisions.answer: Use hxprobe observe <copy> as the only test seam. One count-only JSON contract, no content flags, no sidecars. Prefer a private Rust observation module over a second Python parser or wrapping map output.
decisions.trade_off: A separate structural observer cannot measure the content decoders, but does not construct or format mailbox values. Synthetic fixtures exercise the actual executable.

decisions.question: Which identifiers can be reported?
decisions.answer: Keep object class IDs, block types, typed layout offsets and mail anchor selectors distinct. No numeric property-ID framing is established. wire_field_ids and decoded_field_id_percent remain null; unknown field_id is null.
decisions.trade_off: Unknown entries group unframed remainder by record type. Their frequencies count records with remainder, not discovered numeric property IDs.

decisions.question: What is decoded coverage?
decisions.answer: Partition each verified block payload into outermost bounded envelope candidates, anchor-to-next-anchor mail regions outside those envelopes, and unframed gaps. Decode only the envelope header and class signature (20 bytes) or the mail anchor (16 bytes). Count no heuristic string bytes.
decisions.trade_off: This is a conservative structural lower bound, not total decoder or message recovery coverage. Envelope bytes belong to the record denominator. Nested objects remain opaque. Empty record types are omitted and field-ID denominators are unavailable.

decisions.question: Which output and failure policy?
decisions.answer: Emit only fixed schema labels, structural IDs, wire types and aggregate occurrence/byte counts/percentages. Accumulate before output. Fixed stderr error and exit 2 on invalid header/version/page size, CRC, LZ4, overlapping blocks, object bounds, arguments or I/O.
decisions.trade_off: The scan can refuse ambiguous or damaged data instead of returning partial counts. No paths, content hashes, content strings, record identities or excerpts appear in the report.

decisions.question: Should decompression validation be isolated to observe?
decisions.answer: Fix lz::decode_exact for every caller. Require complete input consumption, forbid literal and match expansion beyond the declared length.
decisions.trade_off: Existing readers now reject malformed blocks they previously accepted. Valid synthetic decoder tests retain their behavior.

decisions.question: How are observation ordering and privacy proved?
decisions.answer: Order block and record types by ID. Order unknown remainder groups by descending affected-record count then record-type ID. Test payload substitution, forbidden fixture strings/UTF-16/hex runs, exact output shape, fixed failures and immutable input.
decisions.trade_off: Synthetic evidence establishes the count-only contract. The orchestrator still owns the private-copy run; no real-store compatibility or coverage is claimed.

decisions.question: How does the branch satisfy delivery preconditions?
decisions.answer: Install ignored local dependencies from the existing lockfiles, including psycopg 3.3.4, and merge origin/main at 17cd3e66 before push. Keep the requested 039a4d05 ancestry; no rebase, force-push or gate bypass.
decisions.trade_off: The first push was refused for freshness and for type errors caused by absent local psycopg. Installing the pinned dependency makes the configured types class pass without a source edit.

decisions.question: Should this criterion repair the progress-board failures?
decisions.answer: No. Reproduce the same two snapshot-size test errors in an untouched detached worktree at 039a4d05 and report them in the PR. Keep the observer criterion scoped.
decisions.trade_off: Broad local CI is not green. Targeted observer, Rust and atlas tests pass. The required hosted checks remain the merge gate.

decisions.question: When is observation unusable?
decisions.answer: Fail the run only for invalid arguments, unreadable input, non-store headers, or unsupported header format. Count CRC, LZ4, truncation, overlap and object-bound failures locally with fixed stage/reason codes and signature ordinals.
decisions.trade_off: Valid store copies can contain unverified candidates. Damaged payloads do not justify losing verified observations.

decisions.question: Which bytes belong in coverage?
decisions.answer: Use all verified decompressed bytes. If structural parsing fails, discard the block-local record counts and count its entire verified payload as unframed.
decisions.trade_off: This loses tentative interpretations from that block but avoids partial credit and inflated coverage. Unverified block bytes have no trusted decompressed size and are excluded.

decisions.question: Does the session include grammar reconciliation?
decisions.answer: The latest assignment authorizes the corrupt-block fix plus ATLAS-GRAMMAR-RECONCILE in the same draft PR. S4 remains separate.
decisions.trade_off: Supersedes the earlier one-criterion stop in D17 for this explicit continuation.

decisions.question: How do assembled constants become atlas grammar?
decisions.answer: Use audit-guided extraction from getter vocabulary and traced dispatch. Read the three audits at exact git revisions, verify SHA-256, match build and all referenced binary hashes to the saved atlas, then emit four reconstructed routes and two host query vocabularies.
decisions.trade_off: No general ARM disassembler or new installed-app scan. A changed binary or build requires a new audit. Retain assembled grammar on extraction only while its exact sources match.

decisions.question: Which source and merge evidence is authoritative?
decisions.answer: Bind PR #2040 merge 913029145c56534c1b6d516bd88a0d43950b5551, PR #2041 head 7432eac46324f2e4db8f9e852d9402c630bfb1af, and PR #2042 head 8f69356aac9162b1b03ffa4b3c7b33e38872cdcb. The last two were open in GitHub readback.
decisions.trade_off: Branch source was explicitly permitted. Reconciliation is provisional until their merge evidence is refreshed; no claim they have landed.

decisions.question: Which grammar differences survive reconciliation?
decisions.answer: Keep literal emails/message/open distinct from reconstructed emails/open/message. Keep recognized host keys distinct from keys read by an action. emails/send consumes no query keys and returns false in the audited canonical branch. account and fallback from select an account; immutableID belongs to open/message.
decisions.trade_off: All reconstructed entries are inferred. Runtime acceptance remains untested, and UI or locked-screen delivery is not inferred from static forwarding.

decisions.question: Which public seams prove reconciliation?
decisions.answer: Use reconcile_surface, extract_surface with a baseline, diff_surface, render_surface, and the actual reconcile CLI over a synthetic git repository. Test byte/hash binding, source/build changes, disagreement, query-key drift, evidence-only drift, and regeneration.
decisions.trade_off: Fixtures prove the extraction contract. The saved real atlas is reconciled against static audit artifacts only; no app or store data is read.

source_study.finding: Maintained Rust reader is unmerged; schema names describe string-run heuristics, not numeric property IDs.
Format evidence covers block CRC/LZ4, UTF-16 runs, ticks and object envelopes. Published recovery counts are not format-byte coverage.
Calendar class 0x006b uses offsets 574 and 582 and variable text heuristics. The body extension reads sidecars; no such read is used by this atlas slice.
Static route survey is unmerged. Its inferred builder vocabulary is not a validated invocation contract.

Cataloged block types 8/16, serialized object envelopes and classes, folder reference offsets, calendar object offsets, and eight mail string-run selector keys. Numeric property-ID framing and first-seen Outlook builds remain unknown.

observation_contract.input_owner: Orchestrator only; desk tests use generated synthetic bytes.
observation_contract.record_bytes: Serialized envelope length including its 10-byte header, mail anchor through next anchor or envelope boundary, or unframed gap. Outermost envelope candidates require marker 5, zero guard, bounded length >=20, and an 8-byte zero class-signature suffix.
observation_contract.decoded_bytes: Unique structural spans only: envelope header plus class signature (20 bytes), or mail anchor (16 bytes). No content interpretation credited.
observation_contract.decoded_byte_percent: 100 * decoded_bytes / total_bytes per observed record type. Absent types are omitted; a zero denominator is unavailable.
observation_contract.field_identifier_policy: fields[].field_id identifies a structural layout position or selector with explicit identifier_kind, never a numeric wire property ID. Values of fields are never emitted.
observation_contract.unknown_fields: One null-field-ID remainder group per affected record type. occurrences counts records with undecoded bytes; unknown_bytes sums their remainder. Descending occurrences then ascending record_type. No claim to have enumerated unframed numeric IDs.
observation_contract.scope: Conservative structural observation, not message recovery, event identities, or full content-decoder coverage.
observation_contract.failure_policy: Fixed {stage, reason_code, block_ordinal} only. Whole-run exit 2 for unusable input. Block-local issues continue, grouped by stage and reason; ordinals are one-based signature positions.
observation_contract.coverage: Total decoded structural bytes / all CRC-and-LZ4-verified payload bytes. Structurally undecodable verified blocks count as wholly unframed.
